A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GenMol and contain complete, readable main text and Appendices A–E. Their text, equations, tables and figures support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original GenMol experiments on molecular generation, hit generation and lead optimization, including numerical results and ablations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original GenMol experimental results, including generation metrics, docking scores and appendix analyses.

M1.justification: The architecture, training objective, confidence sampling, fragment remasking and molecular context guidance are unchanged. Algorithm 1 abbreviates wording without changing its procedure.

E1.justification: Both retain SAFE training, de novo generation, the same fragment-constrained tasks, the 23-task PMO benchmark and lead optimization against five protein targets. Appendix coverage is also unchanged.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain identical baseline membership, including SAFE-GPT, JT-VAE and DiGress in generation experiments, the PMO comparators in Tables 3 and 13–15, and RetMol and Graph GA in Table 4.

E3.justification: The 1,000-molecule de novo evaluation, 100 molecules per drug for fragment-constrained evaluation, 10,000-call PMO budget and lead-optimization constraints remain unchanged. Appendix D retains the same training and evaluation settings.

E4.justification: Section 5.5 and Appendix E retain the same remasking and guidance ablations, quality/diversity analyses, threshold sensitivity analysis, sparse-fragment experiment and generated-molecule examples.

E5.justification: Both report three-run means and standard deviations in the same result tables. No run-count, seed, uncertainty-estimation or significance-testing information is added or revised.

E6.justification: Numerical results and qualitative findings match throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 3 reports GenMol's PMO sum AUC top-10 as 18.362 in both. Figure 1 uses the same embedded image.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, masked-diffusion formulation, loss, guidance equations and Appendix C derivation are unchanged. The fragment-remasking discussion retains the same Gibbs-sampling reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about unified molecular generation, fragment remasking, molecular context guidance and performance across drug-discovery tasks.

C2.justification: Mechanism explanations and result interpretations are unchanged, including the quality/diversity discussion. Appendix A retains the limitation concerning quality loss when unmasking multiple tokens, and the Impact Statement is unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 newly states that GenMol code is available and supplies the NVIDIA-Digital-Bio/genmol repository link in the abstract. v2 gives no GenMol code location. Implementation, hyperparameter and hardware disclosures in Appendix D remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, scholarly citations and reference list retain the same works and research positioning.

P1.justification: Section 4.2 is retitled 'Exploring Chemical Space with GenMol,' Algorithm 1 uses shorter wording, and the abstract gains a code-access sentence. Date/version text changes, while the narrative and section ordering remain stable.

P2.justification: Algorithm 1 becomes more compact through reduced line wrapping. The abstract and several main-text paragraphs reflow, and footer placement shifts slightly. Figures and tables retain their content and structure.

improvement.justification: v3 adds an explicit GenMol code location absent from v2, improving implementation-access documentation. More compact Algorithm 1 formatting also improves readability. These are limited gains; the scientific methods, evidence and limitations remain unchanged.
